source.check: returned without a contest: 'In Downpatrick Rural Council the only division challenged is Killyleagh Urban' (Belfast News-Letter, 27 April 1933, p. 16); chosen a council representative on the Ulster Tourist Development Association at the annual meeting, end of May 1933; moved a motion at the council meeting of 26 August 1933 (round 2, 7 Nov 2026)

note: Triennial election of the Downpatrick rural district council, 1933; polling day for Co. Down, Thursday 25 May 1933. There were no contests: the only division with two nominations was Killyleagh Urban, where Mr. J. H. Wightman withdrew in favour of the sitting member (Belfast News-Letter, 27 April 1933, p. 16, and 4 May 1933, p. 9). The other divisions are not named. Five more divisions (Dunmore, Killinchy, Killyleagh Rural, Leggygowan, Strangford) are recorded from reports of the new council's meetings in its first three months, each with its division from the 1930 return (round 2, 7 Nov 2026). division inferred from the 3 May 1930 return (S. Sharvin, Strangford); the council-meeting report cited names the member as sitting within six months of the election. Returned unopposed.
